card.name: Linking words in science research text
card.fires_on: Small linking words (our, from, to, and, it, new, now) in general science and research-institute prose, mostly about genomes, biotechnology or brain research, just before a description of what the research does.

modes.label: Research aims
modes.description: Small word inside a sentence about what a research institute or project aims to do.
modes.example: NIAID conducts and funds research to improve<< our>> ability to prevent, diagnose, and treat

modes.label: Method purpose
modes.description: The word "to" or "and" after a method or technique, leading to what it is used for.
modes.example: A laboratory test in which cells in a sample of tissue are viewed under a microscope<< to>> look for certain changes in the chromosomes.

modes.label: Scientists are doing
modes.description: Word right after "Scientists are" before an ongoing study.
modes.example: Scientists are<< now>> analyzing the B. anthracis genome

card.writes: It weakly promotes words like classification and diagnosis, so it may push toward classification or diagnosis wording.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in science text that describes what research or a method is meant to achieve.
